column.text: Bitcoin is trading at $73,700, just above the $73,200 support that decides whether this market chops sideways or cascades. Lose that level and the positioning does the rest: the long-to-short skew sits at 2.65, so forced liquidations would feed on themselves. The flows say no one is stepping in. Bitcoin ETFs lost $95.0M on Tuesday 10 Nov, and the seven-day net outflow is $1577.8M. Ether saw $1.3M out on Tuesday 10 Nov, with a seven-day net of $551.1M. Solana's Wednesday 11 Nov outflow was smaller at $5.8M, with $42.8M net over seven days, but the direction is the same. Sentiment is in fear, with the Fear and Greed index at 28, and daily RSI at 34.48 shows oversold readings without buying behind them. Oversold alone is not a long signal in this tape. Derivatives positioning is the tell. Hyperliquid's top accounts are short $639M, while the Lighter whale desk logged only $1.1M of net BTC inflows. Smart money looks like it is hedging downside rather than buying the dip. Stablecoin supply is high, so the liquidity exists, but it is not being deployed into risk. Equities are adding pressure. Nvidia perps fell 10% on Hyperliquid after reports the board may oust Jensen Huang, and macro liquidity is contracting. Treat failed rallies as the better-odds short, and demand a real catalyst, deeply negative funding, or a failed breakdown before taking the long side. Below $73,200, the next move is likely lower and faster.
